newsitem.title: USA: Irish leader criticizes Britain for EMU opposition.
newsitem.headline: Irish leader criticizes Britain for EMU opposition.

text.p: Irish Prime Minister John Bruton predicted on Wednesday that European Economic and Monetary Union would begin as planned on January 1, 1999 and criticized British opposition to the project as being out of step with reality.
"The political arguments are overwhelming for the project going ahead on time," Bruton told reporters.
Bruton, who was visiting Atlanta as part of a five-day U.S. trip, predicted that the single European currency would become a reserve currency like the dollar once convergence had taken place.
The prime minister suggested that British public opinion may not understand the "political benefits of anchoring Germany within a wider European entity.
"In a sense, one must be surprised at that because Britain is a country that suffered a lot in the early part of the century, when Germany wasn't anchored in Europe," Bruton said.

"Britain perhaps has an old 18th Century balance-of-power view of Europe, where they look at Europe as a scene of competing nations where Britain can play the referee. That is an antique view of Europe that isn't in conformity with modern reality," he added.
